title: SIMV: the mandatory breath lands on a supported breath
summary: A patient breathing at 26 a minute on SIMV-PC with 14 mandatory breaths a minute and PS 8. The mandatory clock does not know about the supported breath that just ended, so a mandatory breath keeps starting on the tail of an effort: stacked volumes, a short expiration, a rising baseline. The synchronization window does not help when the effort falls just before it.
objectives: Recognize breath stacking from the mandatory clock: two breaths in one effort, the second time-triggered, with a truncated expiration.
Fix it by letting the patient own the rhythm: pressure support (or assist-control) instead of SIMV.

fix.note: PSV with PS 10: every breath is the patient's own, none is stacked by the clock.
